name: Python

modules.title: Python Foundations
modules.description: Understand how Python runs code and learn the small syntax rules used everywhere.
modules.challenge: Create a small command-line script that asks for a name and prints a formatted greeting.

modules.title: Values, Types & Expressions
modules.description: Work confidently with Python's core scalar values and expression rules.
modules.challenge: Parse two user-entered numbers, calculate a percentage, and format the result clearly.

modules.title: Collections & Comprehensions
modules.description: Choose the right built-in collection and transform data with compact, readable expressions.
modules.challenge: Turn a list of order records into a customer-to-total dictionary while removing duplicate tags.

modules.title: Control Flow
modules.description: Direct program execution with decisions, loops, pattern matching, and useful loop helpers.
modules.challenge: Validate a command, process matching records, and report when no record was found.

modules.title: Functions & Scope
modules.description: Package behavior into clear functions and understand how Python binds arguments and names.
modules.challenge: Design a pricing function with safe defaults, keyword-only options, documentation, and a useful return value.

modules.title: Modules & Packages
modules.description: Split programs into importable files and packages with predictable namespaces.
modules.challenge: Create a package with two modules, expose one public function, and run its CLI entry module safely.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Python
modules.description: Model state and behavior with classes while keeping Python's dynamic object model clear.
modules.challenge: Model an order hierarchy with validated properties, inherited behavior, and a dataclass value object.

modules.title: Python's Object Protocols
modules.description: Make custom objects behave naturally with Python syntax by implementing focused data-model protocols.
modules.challenge: Build a small collection type with useful display, length, iteration, membership, and equality behavior.

modules.title: Errors & Resource Management
modules.description: Handle failures deliberately and guarantee cleanup around files, locks, and other resources.
modules.challenge: Create a parser that reports useful domain errors, preserves the original cause, and always closes its resource.

modules.title: Iterators & Generators
modules.description: Process streams lazily and compose memory-efficient data pipelines.
modules.challenge: Stream a large log file, filter matching records, and aggregate them without loading the whole file.

modules.title: Files, Paths & Serialization
modules.description: Read and write local data safely with explicit paths, encodings, formats, and cleanup.
modules.challenge: Load a UTF-8 CSV file, convert its rows to JSON, and write the output beside the source path.

modules.title: Standard Library Essentials
modules.description: Recognize the batteries already included for common data, date, text, system, and CLI work.
modules.challenge: Build a small command-line report using parsed arguments, grouped records, dates, and regular expressions.

modules.title: Type Hints
modules.description: Describe interfaces for editors and static checkers without changing Python's runtime flexibility.
modules.challenge: Annotate a repository interface and a reusable function while keeping optional and structured data explicit.

modules.title: Testing, Debugging & Logging
modules.description: Build feedback loops that reveal regressions, inspect failures, and explain runtime behavior.
modules.challenge: Test a service with setup, assertions, and a mocked dependency, then investigate one failure with the debugger.

modules.title: Concurrency & Asyncio
modules.description: Choose between threads, processes, futures, and async tasks based on where work waits or computes.
modules.challenge: Fetch several independent resources concurrently with bounded timeouts and graceful cancellation.

modules.title: SQLite & Database Access
modules.description: Persist relational data locally with transactions and parameterized SQL through the standard sqlite3 module.
modules.challenge: Create a users table, insert safely, commit a transaction, and query rows by name.

modules.title: HTTP, APIs & Networking
modules.description: Understand URLs, HTTP requests, JSON APIs, sockets, timeouts, and TLS using the standard library.
modules.challenge: Call a JSON API with each CRUD method, handle HTTP failures, and enforce a timeout.
topics: REST methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH & DELETE

modules.title: Packaging, Performance & Security
modules.description: Ship isolated projects, measure before optimizing, and avoid Python's best-known unsafe defaults.
modules.challenge: Package a small library, profile one workload, and document the security boundaries around its inputs.

1: The interpreter executes Python; the REPL lets you enter one expression or statement at a time.
A .py file stores reusable code that the interpreter can execute as a program.
Indentation is syntax in Python and groups statements under constructs such as if, for, and def.
Assignment binds a name to an object; it does not declare a fixed storage type.
A # comment explains code to people; a docstring documents a module, class, or function.

# Explain why this value matters
def greet():
    """Return a friendly greeting."""
    return "Hello"
print writes text to standard output, while input reads one line from standard input as a string.
A name can be rebound to different object types; id and is concern object identity, not value equality.

value = 42
value = "forty-two"
missing = None
print(missing is None)
2: int stores whole numbers, float stores binary floating-point values, and complex stores real and imaginary parts.
Comparisons produce True or False and can be chained into one readable condition.
None represents the absence of a value and should normally be checked with is or is not.
A string is an immutable Unicode sequence; string methods return new values instead of changing the original.
An f-string evaluates expressions inside braces and formats them directly into text.
bytes is an immutable byte sequence; bytearray is mutable and both are distinct from Unicode text.
Arithmetic, comparison, Boolean, membership, and identity operators follow defined precedence; parentheses make intent explicit.

total = price * count
valid = total > 0 and count in range(1, 100)
3: A list is an ordered, mutable sequence that supports indexed access and in-place updates.
A tuple is an ordered, immutable sequence commonly used for fixed records and multiple return values.
A dictionary maps unique hashable keys to values and preserves insertion order.
A set stores unique hashable values; frozenset is the immutable version and can itself be a dictionary key.
range represents an arithmetic sequence lazily, so it does not build a list of every number.
Slicing selects part of a sequence, while unpacking assigns its elements to several names.

items = [10, 20, 30, 40]
first, *middle, last = items
subset = items[1:3]
A comprehension builds a collection from an iterable with an optional transformation and filter.

squares = [n * n for n in range(10) if n % 2 == 0]
by_id = {user["id"]: user for user in users}
4: An if chain executes the first branch whose condition is truthy and otherwise uses else.
Structural pattern matching compares the shape and values of data and can bind matching parts to names.

match command.split():
    case ["open", filename]:
        print(filename)
    case _:
        print("Unknown")
A for loop asks an iterable for values one at a time instead of managing an index manually.
A while loop repeats as long as its condition remains truthy.
break exits the nearest loop; continue skips directly to its next iteration.
A loop's else block runs only when the loop finishes normally without break.
enumerate pairs items with indexes; zip walks multiple iterables together until the shortest ends.

for index, (name, score) in enumerate(zip(names, scores), start=1):
    print(index, name, score)
5: def creates a function object; return stops that call and sends a value back to its caller.

def total(price, quantity):
    return price * quantity
Arguments may bind by position or by parameter name, making calls either compact or explicit.
A default is evaluated once when def runs, so mutable defaults should usually be replaced with None.

def add_tag(tag, tags=None):
    tags = [] if tags is None else tags
    tags.append(tag)
    return tags
The / and * markers let an API require selected parameters to be passed by position or keyword.

def resize(width, height, /, *, quality=85):
    return width, height, quality
*args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple; **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a dictionary.
Python resolves names through local, enclosing, global, and built-in scopes; nonlocal targets an enclosing function binding.

def counter():
    count = 0
    def increment():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        return count
    return increment
A lambda is a small expression function; docstrings explain behavior and annotations describe intended types without enforcing them.

def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """Return a greeting for name."""
    formatter = lambda value: value.strip().title()
    return f"Hello {formatter(name)}"
6: import loads a module once per interpreter session and binds its module object to a name.

import math
radius = 3
area = math.pi * radius ** 2
from imports selected names into the current namespace; as gives an imported object a local alias.

from pathlib import Path as FilePath
root = FilePath.cwd()
The guard runs code only when the file is executed directly, not when another module imports it.
Python searches built-ins and the directories in sys.path; local filenames can accidentally shadow standard modules.
A package groups modules under a dotted namespace; __init__.py can initialize or define the package's public surface.

shop/
  __init__.py
  pricing.py

from shop.pricing import total
A leading dot imports from the current package hierarchy and should be used only inside a package.

# inside shop/api.py
from .pricing import total
from .models.order import Order
dir reveals available names, help displays documentation, and importlib provides programmatic import utilities.
7: A class defines shared behavior; calling it creates a distinct instance with its own state.

class User:
    pass

user = User()
user.name = "Ada"
__init__ initializes an already-created instance and normally stores constructor values on self.
An instance method receives the instance as self, letting it read and update that object's attributes.
A class method receives cls and can build alternate constructors; a static method is a namespaced function with no automatic instance.
Inheritance reuses and specializes parent behavior; super delegates to the next implementation in the method resolution order.
A property exposes method-backed validation or computation through normal attribute syntax.
@dataclass generates common methods for data-focused classes from annotated fields.
8: Double-underscore methods connect objects to language operations such as addition, indexing, iteration, and context management.
__repr__ aims for an unambiguous developer view; __str__ supplies readable user-facing text.
__eq__ defines value equality; stable immutable values can implement __hash__ for set and dictionary use.
Methods such as __len__, __iter__, __contains__, and __getitem__ let an object participate in built-in container operations.
__enter__ supplies a managed resource and __exit__ performs cleanup when a with block ends.
Implementing __call__ lets an instance be invoked like a function while retaining configuration or state.
A descriptor controls attribute access through __get__, __set__, or __delete__ and powers features such as properties and methods.
9: A syntax error prevents parsing; an exception is an object raised while otherwise valid code executes.

# SyntaxError: invalid grammar
# ValueError: valid code received an unsuitable value
number = int("not-a-number")
A try block protects operations that may fail; matching except clauses handle only the failures they understand.
else runs after a successful try; finally runs whether the operation succeeds, fails, or returns.
raise creates or re-raises an exception when the current operation cannot satisfy its contract.
A domain-specific exception communicates a meaningful failure while remaining compatible with Python's exception hierarchy.

class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    """Raised when an account cannot cover a withdrawal."""
raise ... from ... preserves a cause; ExceptionGroup carries several unrelated failures that except* can handle selectively.
with guarantees a context manager's exit logic; contextlib helps create managers without a full class.
10: An iterable can create an iterator; an iterator remembers traversal state and produces one value at a time.
iter obtains an iterator and next requests its next item, raising StopIteration when exhausted.

iterator = iter(["a", "b"])
first = next(iterator, None)
second = next(iterator, None)
A function containing yield returns a generator that pauses after each produced value and resumes later.
A generator expression uses comprehension syntax but calculates each item only when requested.
total = sum(n * n for n in range(1_000_000))
yield from delegates iteration and value exchange to another iterable or generator.
itertools provides fast building blocks for chaining, grouping, slicing, combining, and repeating iterables.

from itertools import chain, islice
first_ten = list(islice(chain(source_a, source_b), 10))
A lazy pipeline composes generators so only the current values occupy memory.

lines = (line.strip() for line in file)
errors = (line for line in lines if "ERROR" in line)
for error in errors:
    print(error)
11: open selects text or binary mode; text files should specify the intended encoding explicitly.

with open("notes.txt", mode="r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
The file context manager closes the handle even if reading or writing raises an exception.

with open("output.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("Ready\n")
Path represents filesystem paths as objects and provides readable operations for joining, inspecting, reading, and writing.

from pathlib import Path
report = Path("reports") / "daily.txt"
report.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
report.write_text("Ready", encoding="utf-8")
The csv module handles quoting and delimiters so rows are not split incorrectly by hand.

import csv
with open("users.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(file))
json converts supported Python values to interoperable text and parses JSON text back into Python values.

import json
payload = {"name": "Ada", "active": True}
text = json.dumps(payload, indent=2)
restored = json.loads(text)
pickle can preserve Python-specific object graphs but loading untrusted pickle data can execute arbitrary code.

import pickle
# Only load bytes produced by a trusted source.
with open("cache.pkl", "rb") as file:
    cached = pickle.load(file)
tempfile creates race-safe temporary resources; zipfile reads and writes ZIP archives while requiring size and path validation for untrusted input.

from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from zipfile import ZipFile

with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    with ZipFile("bundle.zip", "w") as archive:
        archive.write("report.txt")
12: collections adds specialized containers such as Counter, defaultdict, deque, and namedtuple.

from collections import Counter, deque
counts = Counter("mississippi")
queue = deque(["first", "second"])
next_item = queue.popleft()
functools provides higher-order utilities such as caching, partial application, reduction, and singledispatch.
datetime models dates and times; zoneinfo supplies IANA time-zone rules for aware datetimes.

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
now = datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata"))
re searches and transforms text using patterns; plain string methods are clearer for simple operations.
math offers numerical functions, statistics summarizes numeric data, and Decimal supports explicit base-10 arithmetic rules.

from decimal import Decimal
from statistics import mean
prices = [Decimal("10.20"), Decimal("11.40")]
average = mean(prices)
os and sys expose process and platform facilities; shutil provides higher-level file copying, moving, and archive operations.

import os, shutil, sys
print(os.environ.get("APP_ENV", "dev"))
shutil.copy2("source.txt", "backup.txt")
print(sys.version)
argparse converts command-line strings into validated named values and generates help output.

import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000)
args = parser.parse_args()
13: Parameter and return annotations document intended types and are stored as metadata rather than automatically enforced.

def total(values: list[float]) -> float:
    return sum(values)
Built-in collections accept type arguments that describe the element, key, and value types expected by static tools.
The | operator describes alternatives; T | None means the value may be absent.

def find_user(user_id: int) -> User | None:
    return users.get(user_id)
A type alias gives a meaningful reusable name to a larger type expression.

type UserId = int
type Headers = dict[str, str]

def load(user_id: UserId) -> Headers:
    ...
TypedDict describes dictionaries with known string keys while values remain ordinary dictionaries at runtime.

from typing import TypedDict

class UserPayload(TypedDict):
    id: int
    name: str
A Protocol expresses structural typing: any object with the required members satisfies the interface to a checker.
A type variable preserves relationships between input and output types in reusable functions and classes.

from typing import TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")

def first(items: list[T]) -> T:
    return items[0]
14: A TestCase groups isolated test methods and integrates with Python's standard test runner.
Specific assertions compare actual and expected behavior and produce useful failure messages.
setUp prepares fresh state before each test and tearDown releases resources afterward.
A mock replaces a collaborator so a test can control its result and verify how it was called.

from unittest.mock import Mock
mailer = Mock()
service = SignupService(mailer)
service.signup("ada@example.com")
mailer.send.assert_called_once()
doctest executes interactive-looking examples in docstrings and checks their displayed output.

def add(a, b):
    """
    >>> add(2, 3)
    5
    """
    return a + b
breakpoint pauses execution in the debugger so you can inspect state and step through code.
logging records structured runtime events by severity; warnings report conditions users should address without immediately failing.

import logging, warnings
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.info("order processed", extra={"order_id": 42})
warnings.warn("old_api is deprecated", DeprecationWarning)
15: Threads share memory and suit many I/O-bound tasks; in standard CPython builds the GIL limits simultaneous Python bytecode execution.

from threading import Thread
worker = Thread(target=download, args=(url,))
worker.start()
worker.join()
A lock protects shared critical sections; Queue coordinates producers and consumers safely between threads.

from queue import Queue
from threading import Lock
work = Queue()
lock = Lock()
with lock:
    shared_count += 1
Separate processes have independent memory and can use multiple CPU cores for suitable CPU-bound work.

from multiprocessing import Pool
with Pool() as pool:
    results = pool.map(calculate, inputs)
Executors provide one Future-based API for thread or process pools and collect results as work completes.

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as executor:
    results = list(executor.map(download, urls))
An async function returns a coroutine; await pauses it cooperatively while another task can run.

import asyncio

async def main():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("Ready")

asyncio.run(main())
Tasks schedule coroutines concurrently; TaskGroup provides structured lifetime and failure handling for related tasks.

async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
    tasks = [group.create_task(fetch(url)) for url in urls]
results = [task.result() for task in tasks]
Cancellation asks cooperative tasks to stop; timeout bounds how long an awaited operation may take.
16: A connection owns the database session; execute or a cursor sends SQL and reads result rows.

import sqlite3
connection = sqlite3.connect("app.db")
cursor = connection.cursor()
SQL data-definition statements create tables and indexes just as they do in other relational databases.

connection.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        name TEXT NOT NULL
    )
""")
Placeholders keep values separate from SQL syntax and prevent injection caused by string concatenation.
A transaction groups writes so they either commit together or roll back together after failure.

try:
    connection.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?", (amount, source))
    connection.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?", (amount, target))
    connection.commit()
except sqlite3.Error:
    connection.rollback()
    raise
Using a connection with with commits on normal exit and rolls back when the block raises; close it separately afterward.

with sqlite3.connect("app.db") as connection:
    connection.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expired = 1")
A row factory changes query rows from plain tuples into objects that can support named column access.

connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
row = connection.execute("SELECT id, name FROM users LIMIT 1").fetchone()
print(row["name"])
The backup API copies a live database consistently; closing connections releases file handles and locks.

source = sqlite3.connect("app.db")
target = sqlite3.connect("backup.db")
with target:
    source.backup(target)
source.close()
target.close()
17: urllib.parse separates and combines URL components without fragile manual string splitting.

from urllib.parse import urlencode, urlparse
query = urlencode({"page": 2, "q": "python"})
parsed = urlparse(f"https://example.com/search?{query}")
urlopen sends a request and returns a response context whose bytes should be decoded according to the expected format.

from urllib.request import urlopen
with urlopen("https://api.example.com/users", timeout=5) as response:
    body = response.read().decode("utf-8")
Request accepts an explicit HTTP method; each verb communicates a different retrieval or state-change intent.
# See one tiny request for each HTTP method below.
Encode outgoing JSON to bytes and declare its media type; decode incoming JSON from the response stream.

import json
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
body = json.dumps({"title": "Python"}).encode("utf-8")
request = Request(url, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
    result = json.load(response)
Handle expected HTTP and network failures explicitly and always apply a finite timeout to remote calls.
A socket is a low-level network endpoint; higher-level protocol libraries are usually safer for HTTP and other standard protocols.

import socket
with socket.create_connection(("example.com", 80), timeout=5) as connection:
    connection.sendall(b"HEAD / HTTP/1.0
Host: example.com

")
ssl wraps sockets with certificate validation and encryption; create_default_context provides secure client defaults.

import socket, ssl
context = ssl.create_default_context()
with socket.create_connection(("example.com", 443), timeout=5) as raw:
    with context.wrap_socket(raw, server_hostname="example.com") as secure:
        print(secure.version())
18: A virtual environment gives one project its own interpreter-facing package installation directory.
Running pip through the selected interpreter installs packages into that interpreter's active environment.

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install requests
pyproject.toml declares build-system requirements and standardized project metadata for modern packaging tools.
A source distribution contains source files; a wheel is a built distribution designed for faster, predictable installation.

python -m pip install build
python -m build
# Creates dist/*.tar.gz and dist/*.whl
TestPyPI is a practice registry for verifying built packages and installation steps before publishing the real release to the public Python Package Index.

python -m pip install twine
python -m twine check dist/*
python -m twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*
timeit compares small operations, cProfile finds cumulative runtime hotspots, and tracemalloc traces Python memory allocations.

python -m timeit "sum(range(1000))"
python -m cProfile -s cumulative app.py
python -X tracemalloc app.py
Secure defaults make the safest behavior automatic: keep tokens outside code, reject untrusted pickle data, avoid shell-built commands, and use production-ready servers.

import secrets, subprocess
token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
subprocess.run(["git", "status"], check=True, shell=False)
# Never unpickle untrusted bytes.

async def main():

    print("Ready")

import sqlite3
connection = sqlite3.connect("app.db")

Schema & execute():

""")
Transactions:
try:
    connection.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?", (amount, source))
    connection.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?", (amount, target))
    connection.commit()
except sqlite3.Error:
    connection.rollback()
    raise
Connection context manager:
with sqlite3.connect("app.db") as connection:

URL parsing:
from urllib.parse import urlencode, urlparse
query = urlencode({"page": 2, "q": "python"})

HTTP GET:
from urllib.request import urlopen
with urlopen("https://api.example.com/users", timeout=5) as response:
    body = response.read().decode("utf-8")
REST methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH & DE:
request = Request("https://api.example.com/users/7", method="GET")
with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
    user = json.load(response)
GET asks the API to return a resource without intending to change server state.

body = json.dumps({"name": "Ada"}).encode()
request = Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
    created = json.load(response)
POST submits data so the server can create a resource or perform an action.

body = json.dumps({"name": "Ada Lovelace"}).encode()
request = Request(f"{url}/7", data=body, method="PUT", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
PUT sends the complete replacement representation for the resource at a known URL.

body = json.dumps({"active": True}).encode()
request = Request(f"{url}/7", data=body, method="PATCH", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
PATCH sends only the fields that should change instead of replacing the whole resource.

request = Request(f"{url}/7", method="DELETE")
with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
    print(response.status)
DELETE asks the server to remove the resource identified by the URL.
